records.text: Brother Anton is a Scarlet Crusade emissary at Nijel’s Point, sent to Desolace to fight the Scourge. He speaks of the Crusade’s war against the undead as a cause demanding body and soul, and tests would-be allies through their actions against the undead ravagers. After commending a recruit’s resolve, he directs them to carry his letter to Raleigh the Devout in Southshore, where the Crusade’s work against the plague continues.
Maxton Strang is a mail armor merchant in Nijel’s Point. He offers trade browsing for his goods, including through the armor merchant service.

Maurin Bonesplitter works at Keldran and Thrall's behest to aid the young ruler against the Burning Blade. In Desolace he plans to dismantle the sect and sees its members as corrupted servants of darker powers. His investigation reaches Lord Azrethoc: Maurin studies a demonic contract, recognizes the demon's signature, and seeks what he needs to pierce Azrethoc's wards against scrying. He speaks confidently of magic and dismisses the Burning Blade's own power.

Kolkar Centaurs are one of the groups Warug directs the Magram to kill. His order counts them separately from Kolkar Scouts and Maulers, while placing all three among the Kolkar enemies in the tribes' conflict.

Kolkar Scouts are one of the groups Warug directs the Magram to kill. His order counts them separately from Kolkar Centaurs and Maulers, while placing all three among the Kolkar enemies in the tribes' conflict.

Kolkar Maulers are one of the groups Warug directs the Magram to kill. His order counts them separately from Kolkar Centaurs and Scouts, while placing all three among the Kolkar enemies in the tribes' conflict. In combat, this Mauler can use Thrash.
Kolkar Windchaser is found in Desolace. Its combat responses include spell casts when combat begins and when its health falls to 30–60%.
Kolkar Battle Lord is found in Desolace. Its combat behavior includes a spell cast when combat begins.
Kolkar Destroyer is found in Desolace. Its combat behavior includes a spell cast when combat begins.
Magram Scout is found in Desolace. It shoots when a target is within 5–30 yards.
Magram Outrunner is found in Desolace. When reduced to 1–10% health, it flees for assistance.
Magram Wrangler is found in Desolace. Its combat behavior includes casting Net.
Magram Windchaser is a named creature that uses Lightning Bolt in combat and turns to Healing Wave when badly hurt.
Magram Stormer is a named creature that maintains Lightning Shield both out of combat and during a fight.
Magram Pack Runner is a named creature that flees for assistance when nearly defeated.
Magram Marauder is a named creature that enters Berserker Stance while out of combat.
Magram Mauler is a named creature that flees for assistance when nearly defeated.
Gelkis Outrunner is a named creature that flees for assistance when nearly defeated.
A Gelkis Scout keeps foes at range with Shoot and may flee for help when badly wounded.
A Gelkis Stamper attacks nearby foes with Trample and may flee for help when badly wounded.
A Gelkis Windchaser casts Lightning Bolt in combat and may use Healing Wave when badly wounded.
A Gelkis Earthcaller hurls Fireball in combat and can summon a Gelkis Rumbler while out of combat.
A Gelkis Mauler may flee for help when badly wounded.
A Gelkis Marauder can enter Berserker Stance while out of combat.
The Maraudine Scout is a humanoid combatant. It casts a spell while in combat.
The Maraudine Wrangler is a humanoid combatant. It casts spells in combat and when its health falls between 30% and 60%.
The Maraudine Mauler is a humanoid combatant that uses Thrash.
The Maraudine Windchaser is a humanoid combatant. It casts spells in combat and when its health falls between 15% and 45%.
The Maraudine Stormer is a humanoid.
The Maraudine Marauder is a humanoid.
Gelkis Rumbler is an elemental found in Desolace.
Magram Bonepaw is a beast found in Desolace.

The Burning Blade Augur is a humanoid spellcaster. In combat it can cast Shadow Bolt and Curse of Thorns; when badly hurt, it flees to seek assistance. These behaviors distinguish this augur’s battlefield role.
The Burning Blade Reaver is a humanoid fighter that uses Arcing Smash.
The Burning Blade Adept is a humanoid spellcaster that uses Fireball in combat. This ability marks its role among the Burning Blade creatures.
The Burning Blade Felsworn is a humanoid combatant that can cast Dual Wield when drawn into combat.
A Burning Blade Shadowmage is a humanoid caster that uses Shadow Bolt in combat.
A Burning Blade Summoner can cast Summon Imp while out of combat.
A Hatefury Rogue is a demon that can use Hide while out of combat.
A Hatefury Trickster is a demon that can use Poison in combat.
A Hatefury Felsworn is a demon that can enrage when badly wounded.
A Hatefury Betrayer is a demon that can enrage when badly wounded.
A Hatefury Shadowstalker in Desolace is a combatant that casts Gouge and can become enraged.

A Hatefury Hellcaller is one of the satyrs targeted in Desolace; Takata Steelblade's account says the satyrs have ties to the Burning Blade. It uses Immolate and Rain of Fire, and it can enrage when badly hurt.
A Lesser Infernal is a demon encountered in Desolace that casts a spell when drawn into combat.
A Doomwarder is a demon encountered in Desolace that casts a spell when combat begins. Kreldig Ungor's reagent request seeks Doomwarder blood specifically from a captain or lord.
A Mana Eater is a demon found in Desolace. Kreldig Ungor's reagent request lists Mana Eater brains among the materials sought from local creatures.
A Nether Maiden is a demon in Desolace; Kreldig Ungor's reagent request groups Nether Maidens with Sisters and Sorceresses as sources of nether wings.
A demon Doomwarder Captain whose combat routine includes casting a spell.
A humanoid Mage Hunter whose combat routine includes casting Plague Mind.
A demon Nether Sister whose combat routine includes casting a spell.
A demon sorceress known as Nether Sorceress.
A demon Ley Hunter whose combat routine includes casting a spell.
An elite Deepstrider Giant.
Deepstrider Searchers are giants.
Starving Bonepaws are beasts suffering from hunger.
Rabid Bonepaws are beasts described as rabid.
Dread Swoops are beasts found across several areas.
Dread Flyers are flying beasts found across several areas.
Dread Rippers are beasts found in more than one area.
Carrion Horrors are beasts.
Scorpashi Snappers are beasts found across several areas.
Scorpashi Lashers are beasts found across several areas.
Scorpashi Venomlashes are beasts found across several areas.
Aged Kodos are elderly kodo beasts.
A dying kodo is an animal in Desolace, one of the forms handled by the aged, dying and ancient kodo interaction.
An ancient kodo is an animal found in Desolace, one of the forms handled by the aged, dying and ancient kodo interaction.
A Burning Blade invoker is a combatant whose magic includes Flamestrike and Flame Buffet.
A Slitherblade naga is a combatant who casts a spell while fighting. Naga are among the attackers named in Drulzegar’s account of his crew’s deaths, though that grievance belongs to him.
A Slitherblade sorceress is a combatant who casts a spell in battle. Naga are among the attackers named in Drulzegar’s account of his crew’s deaths, though that grievance belongs to him.
A Slitherblade warrior is a combatant who uses a fighting ability in battle.
A Slitherblade myrmidon is a combatant who casts a spell while fighting. Myrmidons are among the attackers named in Drulzegar’s account of his crew’s deaths, though that grievance belongs to him.
A Slitherblade razortail among the naga of Desolace, it attacks intruders with magic.
A Slitherblade tidehunter of Desolace, it is a hostile naga fighter that attacks with magic.
A Slitherblade oracle of Desolace, it is a hostile naga spellcaster that joins the fight when threatened.
A Slitherblade sea witch of Desolace, it is a hostile naga spellcaster that attacks intruders.
An elder thunder lizard, this beast roams the Barrens and nearby areas and attacks when drawn into combat.
Gritjaw basilisks inhabit Desolace and use Crystalline Slumber in combat.
Hulking Gritjaw basilisks inhabit Desolace and use Crystalline Slumber in combat.

Felgur Twocuts is a Horde agent at Ghost Walker Post, sent to gather intelligence on Desolace's centaur. He directs a campaign against them: disrupt the Kolkar by killing Khan Dez'hepah, then weaken the centaur clans through a bounty on their ears. He expects a long struggle and sees strength and the Horde's banner as ways to deter them from uniting or expanding.

Captain Pentigast seeks alliances with Desolace's centaur clans to contain the threat posed by their wars. He proposes gaining the Gelkis' favor by attacking the Magram, or the Magram's favor by fighting the Gelkis, then directs the player to each clan's representative to pursue an alliance.

Uthek the Wise is a Gelkis shaman who listens to the earth for magical knowledge and seeks draenethyst to strengthen her magic. She directs efforts to weaken the Magram by raiding their meat stores, and mocks Kolkar magic while sending the player to seize their charms. Her praise is tied to practical gains for the Gelkis; after the shard task, she says the player may soon be called a friend.

Warug leads the Magram's campaign against the Gelkis with open contempt for their belief that Theradras protects them. He calls the Magram the strongest and demands attacks on Gelkis resources, including destroying the Tears of Theradras, and the killing of Khan Shaka. His approval is conditional: he likes help against the Gelkis but says the Magram will decide whether the player is strong enough to be a friend.

Gurda Wildmane seeks to turn the centaur clans’ rivalries against them. She offers the player a choice between supporting the Magram against the Gelkis or the Gelkis against the Magram, with the aim of learning how to defeat the clans.
Khan Dez’hepah is the leader of the Kolkar clan in Desolace, one of several centaur clans whose feuding keeps them from uniting against outsiders. He is a forceful combatant who uses magic in battle.

Khan Jehn leads the Magram centaur in Desolace. The Gelkis shaman Uthek the Wise regards the Magram as weakened and calls for Jehn’s death, reflecting the clans’ bitter rivalry. Jehn uses magic in combat.
Khan Shaka is the leader of the Gelkis centaur in Desolace. The Magram spokesman Warug identifies him as the Gelkis Khan and expresses hatred for him, a reflection of the clans’ rivalry.

Kreldig Ungor is a Reclaimer investigating the Karnitol shipwreck and coordinating work in Desolace. He welcomes help with the organization’s recovery jobs, though he is eager to finish the mage Leftwitch’s reagent list and return to Ironforge. An empty chest and unexplained slashes leave him pressing for more information; finding Karnitol’s belongings earns his gratitude and sharpens his hostility toward the naga. He is uncertain about local creatures and their history, and questions the story connecting satyrs to night elves.

Takata Steelblade serves in the Horde campaign against demons and satyrs in Desolace, urging action against the Hatefury and threats to the Warchief’s interests. He frames the fight as a test of honor and dedication, and hopes the Warchief will recognize the campaign’s work. Takata is candid about what he does not know: Lord Azrethoc is unfamiliar to him, so he relies on Maurin’s warning that the demon may seek influence over the Burning Blade. Though he wishes he could confront the demon himself, he stays at his post rather than abandon his clan’s responsibilities. As demonic threats grow, he fears the campaign will keep him from returning to the Warchief.

Vahlarriel Demonslayer is a Darnassian agent sent to find the missing children of House Malem. He is tasked with locating both siblings, but stresses that Dalinda’s safe return matters most and that Tyranis must be assessed before being taken home. When the search points to a Burning Blade fortress, he warns that its demon-serving orcs are dangerous while noting they do not represent most of the Horde.

Tyranis Malem is one of the missing nobles of House Malem, traveling in Desolace with his sister Dalinda. In Dalinda’s account, after the Burning Blade captured them, he tried to impress the orcs with his arcane knowledge. She believes he may seek their secrets and fears he could join them; while she is captive, she does not know his fate.

Dalinda Malem is a missing noble of House Malem, captured with her brother Tyranis by the Burning Blade in Desolace. Fearing she may be sacrificed, she asks for help but says she cannot leave until Tyranis’s fate is known. She believes his growing hunger for arcane knowledge could draw him toward the Burning Blade, a danger she finds deeply troubling. Once she learns what happened, she accepts help to escape, though her gratitude is strained.

Corporal Melkins is an Alliance officer at Nijel's Point who sets a bounty on centaur in Desolace. He frames the hunt as service to the Alliance and a step toward ending the war, and says the bloodshed will save lives. His words give the task a grave, military purpose.

Takata Steelblade admits he has no knowledge of Lord Azrethoc, but repeats Maurin's concern that the demon lord may be seeking influence over the Burning Blade. Takata urges a party to stop him and names him as a target alongside Jugkar Grim'rod. Azrethoc uses spells in combat.

In Desolace, Jugkar Grim'rod is identified by Takata Steelblade as Lord Azrethoc's warlock servant and one of two threats to be ended. Takata urges a party to kill them both. Jugkar responds to combat with spells, including one triggered when an enemy engages him.

Hornizz Brimbuzzle pitches a scheme to collect ghost-o-plasm from the haunted Valley of Bones and sell it to the Magram, using ghost magnets to draw out ghosts. He also worries about his sister Melizza, who he says is always on the go and keeps getting into trouble. He thanks those who help her escape.

Warug's Bodyguard serves as a personal guard for Warug. The supplied records establish the protective role and presence in the area, but provide no supported detail about the guard's personality or history.

Baritanas Skyriver is a hippogryph master who offers flight travel. When threatened, he calls for help, and his assigned aggro response summons an enraged hippogryph. The records offer no further detail about his personal views or history.

Thalon is a wind rider master who offers fast travel. When threatened, he calls for guards, and his assigned aggro response summons an enraged wyvern. The records provide no further detail about his personal views or history.
Janet Hommers runs a food and drink stall and offers goods to browse. The supplied records establish her merchant role but provide no supported detail about her personality or history.

Nijel's Point Guard serves as a guard at Nijel's Point. The records establish the post and show several guards of this named type, but provide no further detail about their individual identities or personalities.
Harnor runs a food and drink stall and offers goods to browse. The supplied records establish his merchant role but provide no supported detail about his personality or history.
Narv Hidecrafter is a leatherworking trainer. He points to kodo hides as the strongest, noting that the kodo have died in the wasteland.
A Ghost Walker Brave in Desolace.
Muuran is a superior macecrafter who offers goods for browsing.
Kireena is a trade goods merchant who offers goods for browsing.

Rokaro is a Horde champion involved in gaining access to Onyxia’s lair. He points the effort toward deception, referring the seeker to Myranda for help, and explains that Drakkisath’s blood can activate the key. His gossip also offers a way to replace a lost Drakefire Amulet.

Innkeeper Lyshaerya offers the familiar comforts of an inn, inviting weary visitors to rest beneath her roof and invoking Elune’s guidance. She also provides goods and has a seasonal trick-or-treat interaction.
Shelgrayn is a stable master who helps with pet care, including stable service and assistance recovering lost companions.
Aboda is a stable master who welcomes adventurers and can help with pet stabling and recovering lost companions.
Innkeeper Sikewa welcomes visitors to the inn and offers goods. Her greeting reflects an open, hospitable manner.

Nataka Longhorn is stationed at Ghost Walker Post, where he welcomes visitors and has needs they may be able to help with. His brother Cliffwatcher sends him a report about unusual centaur activity. Nataka also calls Bloodbelly fish his favorite and asks for some from Jinar'Zillen at Shadowprey Village, saying the post has long lacked cooked fish and that centaur activity leaves him little time to travel.

Jinar'Zillen is a fisherman at Shadowprey Village with shellfish traps beneath the docks. He openly admits that he enjoys doing as little work as possible and asks others to collect shellfish for him, offering Bloodbelly fish in return. He also shares a secret about underwater fissures that provide air, and says he wants to keep the spot from attracting competition for his traps.

Bibbly F'utzbuckle is a goblin bone collector at Kormek's Hut, selling kodo bones through a caravan to Shadowprey Village. He dreams of turning the trade into great wealth and fame, and boasts that his bones can become furniture, instruments, and blasting powder.
An outcast necromancer that casts spells while fighting.
Undead Ravagers inhabit the Valley of Bones in Desolace. Brother Anton names them as targets in the Scarlet Crusade’s campaign against the Scourge.
A humanoid Drysnap crawler that casts a spell in combat.
A humanoid Drysnap pincer that casts two spells in combat.
A kodo associated with the Gizelton Caravan in Desolace.
A wild creature of Desolace, the Whirlwind Ripper attacks intruders and casts a spell when it enters combat.
A wild creature of Desolace, the Whirlwind Stormwalker attacks in combat and uses a spell against its opponents.
A wild creature of Desolace, the Whirlwind Shredder attacks in combat and uses a spell against its opponents.

Smeed Scrabblescrew is a shrewd goblin kodo trader who prizes profit and resents rival Bibbly's success. He says he partnered with Cork and Rigger after learning to tame aged and dying kodos for their caravan. Though he worries that losing the caravan would ruin him, he grumbles at its protection costs and counts on its kodo business to pay. He eagerly celebrates a successful roundup as a step toward getting rich.

Taiga Wisemane works against the demonic threat around Mannoroc Coven. He seeks the Demon Box, which contains the Hand of Iruxos, and directs its use to banish the portals there. His work links the Burning Blade's possession of the box at Thunder Axe Fortress to efforts to stop demons entering the world.

Cork Gizelton runs the Gizelton Caravan with his brother Rigger, leading a traveling business that hires protection when danger threatens its trade. Cork recruits a bodyguard when Kolkar war drums make the route unsafe, and jokes that the brothers have places to go and people to swindle. He also directs customers to his Vendor-Tron 1000, whose fixed prices he touts against bargaining.

Rigger Gizelton co-founded and operates the Gizelton Caravan with his brother Cork. He recruits protection when demons near Mannoroc Coven spook the kodos, and announces when the caravan is moving on. Rigger also maintains the Super-Seller 680 and takes pride in its competition with Cork's Vendor-Tron 1000.

Talendria studies the corruption that stunts Maraudon's plants. She offers a vial whose coating can be filled at the corrupted orange pool and used on Vylestem vines to purge their corruption, though Vyletongue may still control a treated plant. She asks for a sample to help identify the vines, and the liquid returned to her allows her studies to continue. Her words show her concern for the damaged growth and gratitude for help healing it.
A Shadowshard rumbler among the caverns' hostile creatures, it can trample its foes.
Rock Borers are small creatures found in Desolace. They range through several parts of the region.
Rock Worms are creatures found in Desolace, ranging through several parts of the region.

Vark Battlescar is studying the corruption that stunts Maraudon’s plants. He asks for a sample of the Vylestem vine so visitors can recognize it, and uses returned liquid to continue his research. He says the work has healed some plants, though much remains to be done.

Azore Aldamort, an Argent Dawn representative, seeks to recover dangerous naga artifacts and learn from them. He sends a seeker after the Sceptre of Light before the Burning Blade can wield its rumored power to sink cities, and entrusts them with a gem to summon the guardian of the Book of the Ancients. He plans to pass the recovered book to the high council.

Roon Wildmane remembers hunting with Hemet Nesingwary Sr., whose rifle skills impressed him enough that their peoples’ enmity faded during their time together. Roon once promised to welcome Hemet back; now Hemet’s son has taken up the hunt, and Roon sends him a kodo horn as a gift.
Tukk is a general-goods merchant who invites visitors to browse his wares. He is one of Shadowprey Village’s merchants.
Lah'Mawhani trades supplies in Desolace. Visitors can browse her goods.
Malux is a skinning trainer.

Mai'Lahii is a lifelong, enthusiastic fisher who sells fishing supplies and would rather spend her time fishing. When given clam bait, she says fishing was the witch doctor's advice for her headache, and that she already feels better.
Lui'Mala is a fishing trainer.
Wulan is a cooking-supplies merchant who offers goods for browsing.
Hae'Wilani is an axecrafter who offers goods for browsing.

Melizza Brimbuzzle is a trader who tried to do business with the Maraudines in the Valley of Spears and was taken captive. She asks for help escaping and warns that centaurs are preparing to cook her. She says her brother Hornizz can pay for the rescue, and speaks of trying her luck with the more reasonable Gelkis next.
A Shadowprey guardian in Desolace.

Drulzegar Skraghook is a fisherman whose crew was killed in a naga attack near Ranazjar Isle. He carries guilt over surviving and seeks revenge against the naga, asking for help hunting them; his bad knee keeps him from joining the fight himself.
Christi Galvanis is a general-goods vendor in Desolace, where she offers goods for browsing.
A Burning Blade seer who relies on fire magic in combat, using Flamestrike and Flame Buffet.

Willow, of the Twilight’s Hammer, seeks Theradric crystal carvings from Maraudon, presenting the hunt as a chance to study the caverns’ relics. After receiving the requested carvings, he lets slip a more calculating motive: he found the helper easy to persuade and says he will do anything for the right price. His words frame the relics’ powers as something long at rest.

Keeper Marandis is in Desolace with his sisters on a mission for the Cenarion Circle. He seeks powerful outsiders to help recover Zaetar’s remains from Princess Theradras, and sees cooperation among Azeroth’s races as a possible answer to the centaur’s violence. He reflects that Zaetar’s own actions brought suffering and ultimately his death.

Selendra is in Desolace with her sisters to address the ancient tragedy surrounding Zaetar’s death. Though she would prefer they fight the battle themselves, she turns to powerful outsiders because they cannot accomplish their goal alone. She worries that asking for aid may cause further deaths, and plans to seek Marandis’s counsel about Zaetar’s remains.

The Centaur Pariah is an exiled heretic who still believes in his cause: uniting the centaur tribes. He condemns their infighting over scraps of land and insists their heritage is as noble as that of night elves or orcs. To advance his aim, he seeks help from an outsider who is not of any centaur tribe to enter Maraudon, which his people guard as holy ground.
Marandis' Sister is a humanoid in Desolace.
A Burning Blade Nightmare demon found in Desolace.
The Captured Stallion is a captive horse, an animal whose defining context is its captivity.
Prince Kellen is a demon; his encounter includes a moment of rage.
Kaskk is a demon.
Hissperak is a beast.
Giggler is a beast.
Accursed Slitherblade is a humanoid.
Crusty is a powerful creature found in Desolace. Its recorded combat emote announces when it becomes enraged.
The Alliance-aligned Desolace Flame Warden tends the local festival flame. The warden urges visitors to honor Alliance fires and desecrate Horde fires.
The Horde-aligned Desolace Flame Keeper tends the local festival flame. The keeper urges visitors to honor Horde fires and desecrate Alliance fires.

place_records.text: You are in Desolace, a dry land in Kalimdor where both the Alliance and the Horde hold settlements. The Horde keeps Ghost Walker Post and Shadowprey Village, and the Alliance keeps Nijel's Point. Centaur clans fight one another over the dry plains, Hatefury satyrs and Burning Blade cultists haunt the land, and Slitherblade nagas hold sunken ruins off the northern coast.

You are in Kodo Graveyard, a part of Desolace where aged, dying and ancient kodo beasts are found. Hornizz Brimbuzzle schemes to collect ghost-o-plasm from the haunted Valley of Bones and sell it to the Magram, and he worries about his sister Melizza. Carrion Horrors prowl here, and a spirit healer offers a return to life.

You are in Ghost Walker Post, a Horde post in Desolace. Felgur Twocuts runs a campaign against the centaur clans, with a bounty on their ears, while Maurin Bonesplitter works to dismantle the Burning Blade sect here. Gurda Wildmane sets the Magram and the Gelkis against each other.

You are in Sar'theris Strand, a part of Desolace. Selendra and her sisters are here to settle the ancient tragedy of Zaetar's death, and she turns to outsiders because they cannot finish it alone. The centaur hold Zaetar's remains. Slitherblade nagas, drysnap crawlers and raging thunder lizards are the dangers here, and a spirit healer offers a return to life.

You are in Thunder Axe Fortress, a Burning Blade holding in Desolace. Dalinda Malem, a noble of House Malem, is kept here, fearing she may be sacrificed, and she cannot leave until the fate of her brother Tyranis is known. Burning Blade augurs, felsworn and adepts guard the fortress, and dread swoops are found here too.

You are in Mannoroc Coven, a part of Desolace where lesser infernals, nether maidens and sorceresses, and doomwarder captains are the dangers. An exiled centaur heretic, the Centaur Pariah, is here, still pressing his cause of uniting the centaur tribes. A spirit healer offers a return to life.
You are in Sargeron, a part of Desolace where Hatefury satyrs are the danger: hellcallers, felsworn, betrayers, tricksters, rogues and shadowstalkers roam the ground.

You are in Magram Village, a centaur village in Desolace kept by the Magram. Warug leads their campaign against the Gelkis with open contempt for their belief that Theradras protects them, and Magram wranglers, windchasers and stormers are the dangers here. A spirit healer offers a return to life.

You are in Gelkis Village, a centaur village in Desolace where the Gelkis believe Theradras protects them. Uthek the Wise, a Gelkis shaman, listens to the earth for magic and seeks draenethyst, and she directs raids on the Magram's meat stores. Gelkis windchasers, stampers and earthcallers are the local dangers.

You are in the Valley of Spears, a Maraudine centaur valley in Desolace. Melizza Brimbuzzle, a trader, was taken captive here and asks for help escaping. Maraudine wranglers, windchasers and maulers, and Ambereye basilisks and reavers, are the dangers, and the spirit of Kolk can be made to manifest here.

You are in Nijel's Point, the Alliance post in Desolace, with its inn and flight master. Vahlarriel Demonslayer, a Darnassian agent, searches for the missing children of House Malem, and Captain Pentigast seeks alliances with the centaur clans. Corporal Melkins has set a bounty on centaur here.

You are in Kolkar Village, a centaur village of the Kolkar clan in Desolace. Kolkar battle lords, windchasers, maulers and destroyers are the dangers here, and the Kolkar war drums warn travelers when the centaur are near.
You are in Shadowbreak Ravine, a part of Desolace where Burning Blade summoners and invokers, and ley hunters, are the dangers. A Burning Blade nightmare demon and a captured stallion are found here.
You are in The Veiled Sea, an area of Desolace. Drysnap crawlers and drysnap pincers are the dangers here.
You are in Tethris Aran, an area of Desolace. Scorpashi snappers, gritjaw basilisks, whirlwind rippers and dread swoops are the dangers here.

You are in Ethel Rethor, an area of Desolace with a tower and a spirit healer. Azore Aldamort, an Argent Dawn representative, seeks to recover dangerous naga artifacts from the tower. Slitherblade nagas and raging thunder lizards roam the area, along with dread swoops and whirlwind rippers.

You are in Ranazjar Isle, a small island northwest of Ethel Rethor. Slitherblade nagas are the danger here, sea witches and razortails most of all. Rackmore hid a chest on the island, and its two keys were lost.

You are in Kormek's Hut, an area of Desolace. Bibbly F'utzbuckle, a goblin bone collector, sells kodo bones through a caravan to Shadowprey Village and dreams of great wealth and fame from the trade. Willow, of the Twilight's Hammer, is also here, seeking crystal carvings from Maraudon. Raging thunder lizards and gritjaw basilisks are among the dangers here.

You are in Shadowprey Village, a Horde village in Desolace with an inn, a wind rider master and a stable master. Taiga Wisemane works here against the demonic threat around Mannoroc Coven. Drulzegar Skraghook, a fisherman whose crew was killed by nagas near Ranazjar Isle, seeks revenge on the nagas. Vark Battlescar studies the corruption that stunts the plants of Maraudon.

You are in Scrabblescrew's Camp, an area of Desolace. Smeed Scrabblescrew, a shrewd goblin kodo trader, is found here and resents the success of his rival Bibbly. Dread flyers, scorpashi lashers and hulking gritjaw basilisks are the dangers here.
You are in Valley of Bones, an area of Desolace. Undead ravagers are the main danger here, with outcast necromancers and whirlwind shredders also about.
